title: Endgame Mechanics: Which to Do First
summary: How to choose the right Path of Exile 2 end-game system first: a preparation matrix across Fortress, Atlas Masters, Breach, Ritual, Delirium, Abyss, Vaal Temple and Expedition, by clear speed, boss strength, failure cost and reward goal.
description: A hub reference for Path of Exile 2 end-game progression: what each system solves, its start point, end boss and Atlas points, the readiness matrix, playstyle recommendations, a suggested order, failure cost, reward goals, build-problem routing and the 0.5 returning-player view.
prerequisites: A character that can clear and survive Atlas content
Some Atlas Passive Points already banked
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial Team
imageAlt: Waystones, the key to Path of Exile 2 end-game maps

items.title: Which end-game should I do first?
body: Pick by preparation, not by profit. A clear-speed character starts with map-driven systems; a boss-strong character starts with pinnacle gates.
Spend early Atlas points on the system you will actually run, then branch out once points are plentiful.

items.title: Do I need every system?
body: No. Each system solves a different need: crafting, passives, pinnacle bosses, or currency. Run what fits your build and goal.

items.title: What is the cheapest to try?
body: Map-driven systems with a free-exit cost are the safe first step; systems with material or long-reset costs should wait until the character is ready.

sections.title: What each system solves
paragraphs: Fortress and Atlas Masters build your passive and master economy; they are the backbone before deep end-game.
Breach, Ritual, Delirium and Abyss are map-driven pinnacle chains, each ending in its own boss and feeding crafting or currency.
Vaal Temple is a build-and-route system ending in Atziri, while Expedition is a currency-and-site system. Pick the chain that matches your goal.
bullets: Breach / Ritual / Delirium / Abyss = pinnacle chains
Vaal Temple / Expedition = build and currency systems

sections.title: Playstyle recommendations
sections.intro: Match the system to how you play.

cards.title: Clear-speed build
body: Start with Breach and Abyss; both reward fast, mobile clearing and free-exit cost.

cards.title: Boss-focused build
body: Prioritise Trial of Chaos, Sekhemas and Delirium once your single-target and defence are solid.

cards.title: Melee / low move speed
body: Favour Ritual and Vaal Temple over fissure-chasing Abyss until you can keep up with the line.

cards.title: Squishy / SSF
body: Use Fortress and free-exit systems first; avoid material-cost pinnacles until geared.

cards.title: Trade / liquid
body: Run the chain whose currency sells best for your build; Ritual and Delirium feed trade well.

steps.label: Stabilise the Atlas
body: Bank Fortress and early Atlas points; this is the backbone everything else builds on.

steps.label: Pick one map-driven chain
body: Choose Breach or Abyss if clear-speed, Ritual if balanced; run it to its pinnacle to learn the loop.

steps.label: Add a pinnacle trial
body: Once geared, add Trial of Chaos or Sekhemas for Fates, relics and Ascendancy progress.

steps.label: Branch to Delirium / Vaal
body: Add Delirium for Distilled and Simulacrum, Vaal Temple for its long-build route, as points allow.

steps.label: Fill the rest
body: Once points are plentiful, run the remaining chains for their unique rewards and boss unlocks.

sections.title: What players report
sections.intro: Community experiences; treat as strategy, not guaranteed math.

cards.title: Fortress first
body: Players consistently report that banking Fortress points early makes every later system easier.

cards.title: One chain at a time
body: Spreading Atlas points across all chains early is the most common regret.

cards.title: Don't force pinnacles
body: Attempting material-cost pinnacles under-geared burns the most resources.

sections.title: Common problems
paragraphs: If you keep dying in pinnacles, stop forcing them; bank Fortress and free-exit systems first, then gear up.
If Atlas points feel stalled, you likely spread too thin; focus one chain to its points before branching.
If a system feels wrong for your build, switch to the chain that matches your clear or boss strength instead of grinding against it.
